definition: A line or surface joining neighbouring points of a wave that are in phase, such as one crest; neighbouring wavefronts are usually drawn one wavelength apart.
A line showing the direction a wave travels and transfers energy, always perpendicular to the wavefronts.
The return of a wave into its own medium at a boundary, with the angle of reflection equal to the angle of incidence, both measured from the normal.
The change in direction of a wave crossing into a new medium, caused by its change of speed; the frequency stays the same while the wavelength changes.
The spreading of a wave through a gap or round the edge of an obstacle, most noticeable when the gap or obstacle is about one wavelength across.
The speed of light in a vacuum divided by its speed in a medium, $n = \frac{c}{v}$; it has no unit.
The rule for refraction at a boundary, $n_1 \sin\theta_1 = n_2 \sin\theta_2$, with each angle measured between the ray and the normal.
The angle of incidence, in the medium with the larger refractive index, that gives an angle of refraction of $90^{\circ}$; $\sin C = \frac{n_2}{n_1}$.
Reflection of all of a wave back into its medium, which happens when it heads towards a smaller refractive index at an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle.
